messages:
Ethan: FYI — ACME Health is pushing for a hybrid packaging ask. They want a reserved baseline + a separate credit pool that only applies to embeddings, and a discounted overage rate for generation. Need product guidance and a clear SOW snippet by EOD Thu.
Aisha: Quick clarifying Qs — are the credits timebound (monthly/annual)? Should credits be exhausted before reserved overage pricing applies, or run in parallel? Also, do they expect credits to be attached to a specific model or to the ‘embeddings’ product?
Ethan: Credits are monthly, 200k embedding tokens/month, plus 500k reserved tokens for gen+embed baseline. They want credits to be used only for embeddings, and overage to kick in after reserved+credits. Need to show the blended unit economics in the quote.
Priya: We can support scoped credits, but billing needs deterministic precedence rules. Proposal: apply credits scoped-to-product first (embeddings only), then consume reserved commit, then overage rate. Blended rate example (simple):
```
commit_cost = $X
credits_value = $Y
overage_cost = $Z
tokens_total = T
blended_rate = (commit_cost + credits_value + overage_cost) / tokens_total
```
Connor: From runtime perspective: routing by product-type is already doable (we tag requests as generation vs embeddings). Billing pipeline needs a flag to attribute usage to credits before commit buckets — that's a billing + metering change. Estimate: 1 week for billing changes + 3 days for test matrix + 1 week for minor router tweaks + canary. No model infra risk.
billing-bot: Pricing guide: https://redwood.internal/pricing/hybrid-packaging (internal) — see section "Scoped credits" and "blended-rate examples".
Aisha: Draft launch criteria I propose: 1) Product UI to assign/visualize credits by product (embeddings) 2) Billing precedence implemented + unit/integration tests 3) Runtime routing/tagging verified + canary rollout 4) Example SOW language and blended-rate calc in sales deck 5) Contract addendum describing monthly credits and reconciliation.
Priya: I'll prepare 2 blended-rate scenarios for the SOW: conservative (low-credit utilization) and optimistic (high-credit utilization) with numbers. Will add examples of invoice line layout. ETA: tomorrow noon.
Ethan: Sales asks for sample contract clause for credits and overage so legal can review. Also need a short explainer for the customer on how credits are consumed (diagram would be ideal).
Connor: I'll spin up a tracker ticket and include a small API contract addition: `credit_scope=\"embeddings\"` and meter ordering change. Ticket created: INF-4827. I'll add estimated dev hours and test plan.
Aisha: Good. Can we scope a minimal MVP for the pilot to meet their timeline? MVP = billing precedence + runtime tagging + SOW examples + billing UI read-only. No UI write for now. If we can hit that, Ethan can close customer deal as a 2-month pilot.
Priya: Confirmed — we can do billing precedence + read-only UI for pilot. Will label invoice changes as "pilot-compatible" to avoid retro billing complexity.
Ethan: Perfect. I'll tell ACME Health we can run a 2-month pilot with those constraints. Thanks team.
Aisha: Moving to backlog as P1 sales-assisted. I'll attach acceptance criteria: 1) automated test proving credits applied to embeddings first 2) canary rollout without increased error rate 3) billing reports that show credit consumption by day 4) sample SOW and contract clause included in PRD. @Connor please link INF-4827 here.
Connor: Linked INF-4827 in comment thread. Small note: need a short feature flag to turn credit-scoping on per-customer.
Ethan: <@Aisha> thanks. I'll add ACME's legal to the thread after we have the SOW draft. :thumbsup:
Aisha: Nice. PRD checklist: owner (Aisha), eng lead (Connor), finops review (Priya), sales validation (Ethan). Moving to triage board now.
